requirement:
CSS reports only `Comment` attachments. These include `/* … */` blocks and
`//` line comments recognized by the bundled CSS grammar.
rationale:
The requirement `requirements.sdk.sources.css.attachments` has two obligations. CSS reports only `Comment` attachments. Those include `/* … */` blocks and `//` line comments recognized by the bundled CSS grammar.

`tests/outline_content.rs#fn[bundled_languages_classify_only_their_attachment_syntax]` carries the `{test}` reference. Its `test.css` case uses the source `"/* block */\na { color: red; }\n// line\n"`.
- It expects exactly `[(Comment, "/* block */"), (Comment, "// line")]`.
- That covers both the block form and the `//` line form. The `//` comment follows a rule, so it is a real grammar-recognized case.
- The assertion compares the whole list of (kind, text) pairs. An extra attachment, a missing one, or any kind other than `Comment` would fail it. This enforces "only `Comment`".
- The same test uses `Annotation` expectations for Python and TypeScript. That shows the comparison distinguishes kinds, so the CSS assertion is not vacuous.

The rule `a { color: red; }` also gives the test something that could be misclassified, and the test shows it is not reported. I found no other CSS-specific distinction in the text that needs its own test.
